decisions.reason: The supplied publication date, October 13, falls within September 16–October 15. Accept as a new, bounded evaluation of claim completion, not a general ranking of research agents. The saved full text reports 14/90 end-to-end claims met, with only one empirical claim met; Appendix G, Table 16 and its following example distinguish reported success from adequate baselines, calibration tests and latency measurements. These support practical student advice to freeze criteria and audit artifacts ([saved text](data/assets/51fd6c05fff2f297f454f717/9f5a3d8ad0d87cf4b75e0b27ee825183acc71c2811e8bb96e1a59f3c5dca2c35/text.txt), Appendix G). Limits are substantial: one anchor-paper task; an LLM judge with researcher spot-checking rather than demonstrated independent replication; reference-dependent scoring that rewards expected positive outcomes; and possible pretraining exposure (§§3.3, 4.1, 6; Appendix E). Test sessions could inform optimization, so these are not untouched held-out estimates (Appendix B, 'Data and test access'). The shared-backbone comparison does not isolate orchestration: Appendix A, 'Revisions of the workspace instructions,' documents differing instructions, while Appendix F documents different hosts and batches. The 32-GB GPU and 72-hour allowance do not mean equal resource consumption (§4.3; Table 13). Treat improved stagewise results as suggestive, not proof of a single upstream cause. The authors evaluate their own framework; affiliations and financial conflicts are not established in the supplied text. Its linked task package is a reproducibility claim, not an independently inspected replication.

September 16 is inside the inclusive window. The new publication reports an older April 26–May 8 experiment; present the report and its provenance analysis as new evidence, not a newly occurring run. Accept for its concrete Git-based experiment lineage, negative-result records and verification design ([saved text](data/assets/59b2cb8b434efeeb70a133bc/66025228eaffdbf60602a9c3e085782385578f7304cce9751aff2a52b9936729/text.txt), §§3.2, 4.3–4.5). The authors report a development-score reduction from 3.3923 to 1.899044 bpb, but every component was selected on the same 200 texts; this is not held-out generalization. About 98% of the reduction came from the first 18 scored contributions, and the final improvement was below cross-hardware variation (§4.5, 'Trajectory' and 'Primary result'). The 165 verifications are other-account checks within one project, not independent research-team replication; one confirmation exceeded the stated approximate tolerance (§4.5, 'Lineage and reproduction'). Missing evaluator logs and dependency/data pins, plus the authors' explicit statement that they did not rerun the winner, limit reproducibility (§4.8). Human prompt and server changes, manual sessions, shared process visibility and mutable index records qualify claims of autonomous coordination (§§4.2, 4.7). Each worker had an 80-GB GPU, but no matched efficiency comparison establishes compute savings (§4.2; conclusion). Students can adopt provenance and failure logging without assuming this scale or performance transfers. The platform builders report their own experiment, creating an evaluative interest; financial conflicts are unspecified. Retain these caveats rather than treating account counts as corroborating independent sources.

The September 24 publication is in-window; it reports a preceding twelve-week campaign rather than dating every experiment to this window. Accept as a practitioner case study of costly failures, persistent memory and metric design, with performance claims attributed to the authors. Concrete examples include eleven consecutive evaluation timeouts, repeated failed configurations and coherence gains obtained through unusable singleton clusters ([saved text](data/assets/7082835cef4c8540dcb8d480/7d04403761d8cb23614022d48ddb879a6de4fb7f5af821bb1d1d2cb773d97ec4/text.txt), §§III-A–III-E). These make cost-sensitive checks and human evaluation design relevant to smaller student experiments; the authors themselves call the cost principle a two-data-point observation (§VI). Report the 1.82× Recall@6 lift as a peak: the across-date mean is 6.18%, or 1.63× the hand-tuned baseline, across eleven dates; these remain offline proxies (§§V-A, V-E). Examine two internal tensions explicitly: §V-E says an immutable evaluator prevents metric gaming, yet §III-E documents gaming without evaluator edits; §V-A claims agent additions establish causality, while §VI admits observational transitions cannot exclude accumulated search. Neither unsuccessful search nor unmet usability targets proves an inherent tradeoff. System B used human pivots and one researcher agent, so its gain does not independently validate the three-agent framework (§IV, Table III; §V-C). Proprietary purchase data and unavailable underlying experiment records prevent independent verification of numerical gains; no independent replication or online outcome validation is supplied (Reproducibility; §VI, 'Limitations'). Accept the inspectable methodological account, not established efficacy. This is an Amazon deployment account using Amazon Bedrock, with an organizational commercial interest; two internal workstreams are not independent external corroboration (§I; Acknowledgment).

October 11 is in-window, but recency does not make this general product roundup useful evidence for the series. The 'AI releases' and 'AI research' lists summarize announcements without inspectable experimental methods, budgets, baselines or results. The potentially relevant Epoch and ATLAS entries are only link descriptions; their original reports are not supplied and cannot substantiate research-agent claims here ([saved text](data/assets/78deb02bb43b9240c74487b3/4c16684f04ac89de0cfd2e9942cde9c20a91e0d7aa7d934da6ede6eaa2463817/text.txt), 'AI releases,' 'AI research' and 'AI resources'). This item adds no original experimental evidence or demonstrated methodological novelty for students. Its 'All my paid goodies in one place' section establishes a subscription-promotion interest; sponsorship or affiliate relationships are not established. Reject the roundup rather than treating its linked announcements as independently corroborated sources.
